clue.text: A lady's case for agreement

definitions.meaning: a small hinged case holding face powder and a mirror, carried in a handbag
a formal pact or treaty between parties

explanation.surface: Someone seems to argue the merits of a woman's legal claim.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a powder case and a pact, two unrelated senses sharing one spelling.

clue.text: A drug designed to support retired conservative members of group

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: someone retired is old

indicators.note: designed means put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A medicine created for elderly pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' turns A DRUG into GUARD, placed under OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the long-standing traditionalist members of any party or club, resistant to change.

clue.text: Post Office holding new item in tropical fruit

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece sits inside the other
new signals the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A post office stocks a new line of exotic produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ITEM IN into IMIENT, held by P and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet red pepper, the fruit of a tropical American plant, used to stuff olives.

clue.text: Doctor and diplomat overseas go brown, with time

parts.note: a consul is a diplomat stationed abroad
to tan is to go brown in the sun

explanation.surface: A medic and an envoy abroad eventually get suntans.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior hospital doctor in Britain holds the title consultant; a specific kind of doctor.

clue.text: Women supply weapons and cordial

parts.note: to arm is to equip with weapons

explanation.surface: Women hand out guns and a fruit drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cordial' looks like the drink, but it is the adjective meaning friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe a friendly, heartfelt manner.

clue.text: Physical consequence of being let out in fast car?

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a Jag is a Jaguar, a fast car

indicators.note: out signals the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A passenger suffers after being released from a speedy vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns LET into ETL, placed in JAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatigue after crossing time zones is a bodily after-effect of flying.

clue.text: Calm and peaceful, as any loch could be

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A Scottish lake is described as tranquil.
explanation.definitionFit: Halcyon days are tranquil and happy, from a mythical bird said to calm the seas.

clue.text: A couple of lines on issue raised may be so far unsurpassed

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines give LL

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word reads it upwards, backwards

parts.note: to issue is to emit

explanation.surface: Text about a published edition might be the best yet.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-time record is the best ever achieved up to now.

clue.text: Vulgar party game

parts.note: base means low, coarse, vulgar
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: A rowdy celebration features some sort of contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The American bat-and-ball sport is an example of a game.

clue.text: A chap employed by a newspaper firm

indicators.note: being employed by a firm puts you inside it, so these letters go within the others

parts.note: DT is short for the Daily Telegraph, the paper this puzzle appears in
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man is described as working at a press company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a noun for the employer, but it is the adjective defining the answer. DT, for the Daily Telegraph, is the setter's own paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone unyielding, refusing to change their stance; synonyms.

clue.text: Suggested facility with no protection

indicators.note: the outer letters form a protective shell around the word, and here that shell is stripped away

parts.note: facility means ease, simplicity

explanation.surface: Someone hints that a building lacks any security measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facility' reads as a building but means ease. 'with no protection' removes its outer letters S and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implied rather than stated outright is suggested; the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Popular string instrument at sea oddly dropped — undamaged

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a viola is a bowed string instrument

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters keeps only the even ones

explanation.surface: A well-liked violin-type instrument survives a voyage intact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly dropped' keeps the 2nd and 4th letters of AT SEA, T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left intact and unharmed is inviolate; synonyms.

clue.text: Foreign Office desk

definitions.meaning: the French word for an office, borrowed into English, so an office from abroad

explanation.definitionFit: The word is French for office and also names a writing desk with drawers.

clue.text: Fuming, mostly with northern man getting married for family space

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: fuming with anger means livid
a groom is the man at his own wedding

explanation.surface: A northerner is seething about his wedding plans.
explanation.definitionFit: The lounge is the shared room where a household gathers, a cryptic phrase for it.

clue.text: Show on TV is next to …

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next one, but each is solved separately.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian soap is named for people living near each other, and the verb means adjoins.

clue.text: Legal document comedian must keep right

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a wit is a clever, funny person

explanation.surface: A comic must retain the rights to a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written court order is a kind of legal document.

clue.text: Musical performances from people who speak publicly about Nixon regularly

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the speakers go round the other letters

parts.note: orators are public speakers

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals from the name gives every second one

explanation.surface: Speech-makers discuss the American president Nixon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd and 4th letters of Nixon, I and O, which go inside ORATORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Large-scale sacred choral works such as Handel's Messiah are musical performances.

clue.text: … take out of production and harden fresh ideas

parts.note: to set is to harden, as concrete does

indicators.note: fresh signals a new arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Farmland is withdrawn and new thinking becomes fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers set aside fields, withdrawing them from cultivation under subsidy schemes.

clue.text: Virgin adopts endless regulation for treatment on foot

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pure means virginal, chaste

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: an edict is an official order or regulation

explanation.surface: A newcomer takes up new rules for walking care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts EDICT to EDIC, which PURE 'adopts'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic care session for the toenails and feet is a foot treatment.

clue.text: Sour look on a day for transfer

parts.note: milk gone sour is off
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone gives a bitter glance on a particular day of a move.
explanation.definitionFit: To unload goods or pass a burden to someone else is to transfer it.

clue.text: Tacky books dismissed by some peers

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: viscounts are one rank of British peer
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Members of the nobility reject cheap, vulgar reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tacky' looks like cheap taste, but here it means sticky.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe a thick, sticky substance.

clue.text: Positive response on European sight

definitions.note: a singular noun for the faculty of vision, matched by the plural organs

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: yes is an affirmative reply

explanation.surface: A Continental gives an affirmative answer about a view.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes stand for the faculty of vision, as in having good eyes; a metonym.

clue.text: Gentle touch required in case of foolish pilot's route

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: a light pat is a gentle touch

explanation.surface: A daft airman needs a soft hand to steer his course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of foolish' gives F and H, which hold LIGHT PAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's planned course through the sky is the route its pilot flies.

clue.text: Barrier hotel ruled out

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: out signals the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A hotel has been ruled off-limits by a blockade.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence jumped in racing, or any obstacle, is a barrier.

clue.text: Go round centre of city

parts.note: a police officer's round is his beat

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, dropping the ends

explanation.surface: A traveller is told to circle the middle of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of city' gives IT, the middle two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal command to leave, like 'scram' or 'clear off'.

clue.text: Slash price of delicate material?

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether to cut the cost of fine fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slash price' suggests a sale, but 'Slash' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut or tear flesh roughly is to slash it; synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: Hit 100 thousand!

parts.note: a ton is a hundred, as in cricket runs

explanation.surface: A batsman scores a hundred and a thousand!
explanation.definitionFit: Tonk is British slang for striking hard, especially a ball in cricket.

clue.text: Hopping mad, seeing evidence of debts attached to coat

indicators.note: one piece is joined on to the end of the other

parts.note: an animal's coat is its fur
IOUs are written acknowledgements of money owed

explanation.surface: Someone is livid at finding unpaid notes pinned to a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopping mad is an idiom for extremely angry, enraged.

clue.text: A diver's source of inspiration?

parts.note: inspiration here means breathing in, and a diver draws breath from a tank of compressed air

explanation.definitionFit: The underwater breathing apparatus supplies air for a diver to inhale, so it literally provides inspiration.

clue.text: Strangely rude about the girl being guided

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the other piece
strangely signals the letters are arranged oddly

parts.note: she refers to a girl

explanation.surface: A girl is escorted while being impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' turns RUDE into URED, which goes 'about' SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shown to a seat by an attendant is being led or guided.
